title: Kids With Autism Face a Much Higher Drowning Risk
hook: Children with autism can be up to 160 times more likely than their peers to drown. Florida is now funding swim lessons specifically to close that gap.
key_points: Kids with autism can be up to 160 times more likely than other children to drown.
Wandering behavior common in autism raises the odds of unsupervised access to water.
Florida is dedicating state money to a voucher program prioritizing swim lessons for autistic kids.
Formal swim instruction and constant supervision near water are the clearest protective steps.
content_html: Drowning is a leading cause of death for children, and kids with autism face a strikingly higher risk — reported as up to 160 times more likely than their peers, per NPR. Much of that gap traces back to wandering, a common autism-related behavior that can put a child near water without anyone realizing it.
extra_html: Florida is responding with a state-funded voucher program that prioritizes swim lessons for children with autism, betting that formal instruction can close a gap that supervision alone doesn't fully solve. For any family navigating autism, the practical takeaways NPR highlights are straightforward: treat access to pools, tubs, and open water as a serious wandering risk, and get kids into structured swim lessons early rather than assuming general caution is enough.
